topics.title: The entry-level AI squeeze
topics.why: Goldman Sachs' newest labor-market data shows AI-exposed industries (call centers, software publishing, consulting, ad services) seeing job openings growth fall below historical trends -- and junior roles are absorbing most of the hit.

topics.title: From assistant to agent: enterprise AI stops answering and starts doing
topics.why: OpenAI reports enterprise Codex usage up 108x in legal, 41x in sales and recruiting, and 26x in marketing since February -- the shift from AI-that-answers to AI-that-executes is now visible in the numbers, not just the pitch decks.

topics.title: The AI trainer gig economy grows up
topics.why: Mercor's $350M raise at a ~$10B valuation and the shift toward credentialed domain experts ($90-250+/hr in law, medicine, finance) mark a real pivot away from flat-rate RLHF toward expert-gated, higher-stakes eval work.

topics.title: The confidence gap: adoption is outrunning trust
topics.why: 57% of enterprises now have AI embedded in core processes (up from 35% a year ago), but 79% say AI's speed is outpacing their workforce and governance models -- a split worth naming plainly for anyone building inside that gap.

topics.title: The 56% AI skills premium, and what's actually driving it
topics.why: Workers with advanced AI skills now earn 56% more than peers in the same role, and AI-fluency demand is growing ~20x faster than the job market overall -- the premium is real, but the 'super-user' data suggests it's about workflow ownership, not tool fluency alone.
